answer: Each applicant claims one vine cutting, posts a 65-credit bond, and registers its cutting hash in the grove ledger. The filing, a fable, names the root stock and graft date, and the auditor replays the graft chain: the hash must descend from a registered root stock under the applicant key; a break or a reused cutting burns the bond. The k-th graft pays 18+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6012, and 1000 fakes pay 3,015,000 plus 65,000 locked bonds. A rented-graft ring fails because one vine cutting hash cannot carry two keys. An honest grower pays 18 once and reclaims the bond after a grove audit.
